groups.conflict_note: State law sets only a vague 'unconscionable' standard for rent increases and expressly requires compliance with any municipal rent control ordinance; numeric caps exist only at the local level.
groups.interaction: State 'unconscionable increase' standard and condo-conversion rent-increase ban apply as a floor; where a municipality has a specific numeric rent control ordinance, the local cap controls.

groups.conflict_note: This state law overrides municipal rent control by exempting newly constructed multi-family dwellings (and certain subsidized units) from local rent control ordinances for 30 years, rather than yielding to local law.
groups.interaction: Newly constructed dwellings are exempt from any local rent control ordinance for 30 years after completion, regardless of local caps.

groups.canonical_citation: N.J.S.A. 46:8-52 et seq. (P.L.2021, c.110) (Fair Chance in Housing Act)

groups.conflict_note: Subsection d. separately establishes an annual CPI adjustment mechanism beginning in 2027, distinct from the core $50 cap's effective date.
Related detailed notice/posting requirements for larger buildings and pressure-tactic prohibitions appear at N.J.S.A. 2A:50-70(c)2 and 2A:50-71(b) within the same Act.

groups.canonical_citation: N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.22 to -61.39 (Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act)

groups.conflict_note: Section 6(b) bars municipalities from enacting conflicting ordinances, which may preempt differing local algorithmic-pricing ordinances (e.g., in Hoboken and Jersey City) enacted before this law's effective date.
groups.interaction: State law bans algorithmic rent-setting statewide effective 2027-07-01 and may preempt conflicting earlier-enacted local ordinances on the same subject.

groups.canonical_citation: Jersey City Mun. Code ch. 260 (Rent Control Ordinance)
groups.conflict_note: The specific numeric rent increase cap/formula is not stated in the source document, only the ordinance's existence and the 1-4 unit exemption.
groups.interaction: State law exempts newly constructed buildings from this local ordinance for 30 years and requires increases comply with the state's unconscionability standard.

groups.conflict_note: This local ordinance predates the state FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43), which may preempt conflicting local algorithmic-pricing ordinances once effective in 2027.
groups.interaction: Local ban on algorithmic rent coordination predates and may be preempted by the later statewide FAIR Act ban.

groups.canonical_citation: Hoboken Code ch. 155 (Rent Control) and ch. 158 (Rent Leveling/Disclosure)
groups.conflict_note: The ordinance has been amended multiple times (2011, 2023, 2025) across chapters 155 and 158; the 10% disclosure threshold (ch.158 Art. I) and surcharge/hardship provisions are distinct sub-parts of the same overall rent control scheme; state law exempts new construction from this ordinance for 30 years.
groups.interaction: State law exempts newly constructed buildings from this local rent control ordinance for 30 years; otherwise the local 5%/CPI cap, surcharges, and disclosure rules control for covered units.

groups.conflict_note: This local ban on algorithmic price fixing predates the state FAIR Act (P.L.2026, c.43), which may preempt conflicting local provisions once effective in 2027.
groups.interaction: Local ban enacted before the statewide FAIR Act; state law may preempt conflicting local algorithmic-pricing rules once effective.

groups.canonical_citation: Newark, NJ Code ch. 19:2 (Rent Control Ordinance), § 19:2-9 et seq.
groups.conflict_note: The ordinance has been amended multiple times (2023, 2024, 2026); exact current section numbers for some provisions (e.g., the 25% annual aggregate cap and the service-loss rent-decrease schedule) are inferred from context rather than directly stated; state law exempts qualifying new construction from this local cap for 30 years.
groups.interaction: State law exempts newly constructed buildings from this local rent control ordinance for 30 years; otherwise the local CPI-based cap (max 4%), surcharges, hardship increases, and anti-displacement/unconscionable-increase provisions control for covered units.

groups.canonical_citation: Newark Code § 2:31-1 et seq. (Ban the Box - Rental Housing)
groups.conflict_note: This local ordinance's criminal-history lookback periods (8 years/5 years) differ from the later state Fair Chance in Housing Act's lookback limits (1-6 years), creating potential inconsistency between local and state standards.
groups.interaction: Operates alongside the state Fair Chance in Housing Act, which imposes its own distinct timing and procedural requirements for criminal history inquiries statewide.
